published_source: Printed Table 1, column (3) Excluding industries where <1% of firms have APIs of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2023.4968.pdf, p. 7131, main text), read Nov 4 2026; equals the authors' code output to the printed decimals. Earlier: Authors' Stata log logs/2_stata_regressions.smcl and esttab output tables/TABLE_01_pre_post_log_market_value_baseline.tex in the package; no article text or PDF in the project, so the values are checked against the authors' code output only, not against the printed article.
column: (3) Excluding Industries with Fewer than 1% Firms with APIs
replication_status: exact (authors' code output 0.37672 (0.0856291), N 127796, equals printed Table 1 column (3) 0.377 (0.0856), N 127,796, to the printed decimals; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Benzell, Hersh and Van Alstyne (2023), Table 1 (3) Excluding Industries with Fewer than 1% Firms with APIs: reghdfe ln_mkt_val api_treat_post if api_ever_treated_01 == 1, absorb(gvkey date) vce(cluster gvkey) (replication_package_MS-INS-22-01020/programs/2_stata_regressions.do line 401); sample: api_ever_treated_01 == 1 (2-digit SIC industries whose adopter share exceeds 1%, computed on the analysis sample). Outcome ln_mkt_val = log firm market value, no controls, no weights. fixest on the authors' row-level sample reproduces b = 0.376720, SE = 0.0856291, N = 127796 (exact). Outcome SD in the run_spec regression sample (weighted, population) = 2.50041, so the expected standardized TWFE is 0.150663. Data: shipped analysis_dataset/api_compustat_gvkey_quarterly_sictreated.dta (Compustat x ProgrammableWeb firm-quarters, original data), rebuilt in R following 2_stata_regressions.do lines 121-262: drop if ln_mkt_val missing or sic_code empty (133,292 firm-quarters, 4,748 firms, 2007Q1-2020Q3 = Stata %tq 188-242, 55 quarters); date = quarterly(year, quarter); api_treat_date_q = qofd(api_treat_date); sinceAPIq = date - api_treat_date_q; dmerge gvkey dateq using hacks.dta (1:m, _merge == 2 dropped) adds 11 duplicate firm-quarters (11 firm-quarters each matched to two PRC breach events; 133,303 rows). Prepared file ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2023.4968/api_panel_collapsed.rds collapses the 11 merge duplicates to one row per firm-quarter (outcome = mean of the duplicated rows; all other columns identical within the duplicates) with frequency weight w_mergedup = number of authors' rows (2 for 11 firm-quarters, 1 otherwise). This reproduces the authors' row-level OLS exactly (identical normal equations and cluster scores) while giving the runner a proper firm-quarter panel: with the duplicates kept, estimators.R's anyDuplicated(id, t) > 0 test would switch CSA to the repeated-cross-section att_gt(panel = FALSE) path for a firm panel. The authors' row-level sample is kept in api_panel_authors_sample.rds. Treatment: gvar = api_treat_date_q (quarter of first public API); api_treat_post equals 1[date >= api_treat_date_q] in every row (verified), 0 for the 4,569 never-adopters, absorbing (no switch-offs). Full sample: 179 adopters with 50 distinct adoption quarters (2005-2019); 100 switchers in 41 cohorts observed before and after adoption; 74 adopters treated at their first observed quarter (always-treated; 16 adopted before 2007Q1 and are dated at 2007Q1 by run_spec's gvar mapping); 5 adopt after their last observation. Never-treated firms: 96.2% of firms, 95.0% of rows. Unbalanced panel (entry/exit), so run_spec uses the composition-fixed CSA cells. Cluster gvkey as published. reghdfe drops 101 singletons (published N); run_spec keeps them (same point estimate).
